learningObjective: Identify correct statements about executing an AOTInductor-compiled artifact at runtime.
stem: Which statements about running an AOTInductor-compiled artifact are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The artifact automatically links against `libtorch.so` at runtime and requires the full PyTorch binary distribution to be present on the deployment machine; without libtorch the .so cannot be loaded.

The artifact exposes a C-ABI entry function; callers pass input tensors as device-memory pointers with shape/stride metadata and receive output tensors similarly, without requiring the Python runtime.
The artifact still requires the Inductor compiler at runtime; on first invocation Inductor is re-invoked to lower the graph, which is what allows the artifact to accept new shapes at inference time.

The artifact bundles the generated Triton/CUDA kernels needed to execute the model, and the runtime loads them via the shared library's loader; no separate kernel binaries need to be shipped alongside the .so.

explanation: B: AOTInductor exposes a stable C interface for driving the compiled model, without requiring Python. D: The generated kernels are bundled with the .so and dispatched by the artifact itself. C is wrong: the whole point of AOT is that Inductor is not needed at runtime; new shapes work only if the artifact was built with dynamic dims. A is wrong: AOTInductor is designed to avoid a full libtorch dependency; it links against a minimal C shim.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: the artifact links against a minimal C shim, not full libtorch.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: stable C interface for calling into the artifact.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: Inductor is not present at runtime; artifacts run without the compiler.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: kernels are bundled into the artifact.

assumptions: The artifact was built for the target GPU architecture.
nonImplications: Does not imply arbitrary shapes are supported; only those declared as dynamic at build time.
Does not imply the C ABI has been permanently frozen; the interface is stable within a major version but may evolve.
